interface.signature: def KDistanceNodes(root: TreeNode, target: int, k: int) -> list[int]: ...

preconditions.expression: isinstance(root, TreeNode) or root is None
preconditions.description: root is either a TreeNode instance or None, representing an empty tree.
target is an integer within the valid node data range [1, 10^4].
k is an integer within the valid distance range [1, 20].

preconditions.expression: all(isinstance(node.val, int) and 1 <= node.val <= 10**4 for node in [root] if node is not None)
preconditions.description: Every node in the tree has an integer value within the valid range [1, 10^4].

postconditions.expression: all(isinstance(node, int) and 1 <= node <= 10**4 for node in return_value)
postconditions.description: Every element in the returned list is a valid node value within the range [1, 10^4].

postconditions.expression: len(return_value) == len({node for node in return_value})
postconditions.description: The returned list contains no duplicate node values.

postconditions.expression: all(node in {n.val for n in [root] if n is not None} for node in return_value)
postconditions.description: Every node value in the returned list exists in the original tree.

postconditions.expression: all(any((ancestor == target and distance == k) or (ancestor != target and distance == k) for ancestor, distance in get_ancestor_distances(root, target)) for node in return_value)
postconditions.description: Every node in the returned list is at exactly distance k from the target node, where distance is computed as the shortest path length in the tree (including parent-child and child-parent traversals).
The returned list is sorted in ascending order.
